subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 24-year-old man has had three episodes of renal colic in the past 2 years. A plain radiograph shows a radiopaque stone in the left ureter, and urine microscopy shows flat hexagonal crystals. A urinary sodium cyanide-nitroprusside test is positive. Serum uric acid and serum calcium are normal, and he has no history of bowel disease.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate long-term management of this condition?

options.text: Urinary alkalinization with potassium citrate, high fluid intake, and penicillamine
Dietary oxalate restriction with pyridoxine supplementation
A thiazide diuretic with sodium restriction
A low-purine diet with urinary acidification

explanation_correct: Cystinuria is an autosomal recessive defect of the proximal tubular and intestinal transporter for cystine, ornithine, lysine, and arginine (COLA), which leads to recurrent hexagonal cystine stones. Cystine is poorly soluble in acidic urine, so treatment aims to increase its solubility with urinary alkalinization using potassium citrate, good hydration, chelation with penicillamine, and a diet low in methionine.

explanation_incorrect.B: Calcium oxalate stones are managed with hydration and, in hyperoxaluria, oxalate restriction and pyridoxine, but oxalate crystals are not hexagonal and the nitroprusside test would not be positive.
explanation_incorrect.C: Allopurinol reduces uric acid production for radiolucent urate stones, and urinary acidification would further reduce cystine solubility and worsen stone formation.
explanation_incorrect.D: Thiazides reduce urinary calcium excretion and prevent calcium stones, but they do not correct the cystine transport defect.
explanation_incorrect.E: Purine restriction addresses urate stones; acidifying the urine would precipitate cystine and is the opposite of the desired therapy.

educationalObjective: Cystinuria causes hexagonal cystine stones that are treated by alkalinizing the urine, increasing fluid intake, chelating cystine with penicillamine, and restricting dietary methionine.
